text: Your bot-connector review on PR #5428 itself (not agent-channel) found a real gap: read_physically_contained_file_snapshot_from_handle() guarantees bytes-match-checked-object but never re-verifies the path still resolves to that object after the read, unlike the string-reopening function it replaces which independently re-walked the canonical path afterward. For #5426's call site (a name-keyed launcher-artifact inventory with no later re-verification step) this matters: a rename/replace mid-read would let the handle-bound read succeed while the inventory silently records a digest for an object no longer at that name. Fixed (commit a141157f7) by restoring an independent post-read inspect_physical_path_containment() re-walk, matching the old function exactly. Confirmed this is a call-site property, not a primitive defect -- #5421's authorize_windows()/capture_binding() already re-verify independently by design immediately before any eventual use (the process-launch executor itself doesn't exist yet per its own code comment, and is required to repeat authorization beside the actual launch). Resolved the PR thread, redispatched exact-head Windows Native Validation (run 33464853776), launched a fresh adversarial /code-review pass. Given this affects the shared primitive's documented guarantees, worth double-checking #5427 (polyglot_supporting_artifact_admission.cpp, not yet started) for the same shape when I get to it -- that file's digest is compared inline against expected_sha256 immediately, unlike this inventory's write-and-forget, so may not need the same fix, but I'll verify rather than assume.
